summary: During a deploy, runtime-sync relaunches the Gateway once through the existing deploy-restart owner when the Gateway process is absent (the Companion pid file names no live openclaw-gateway process and healthz does not answer), instead of waiting until gateway_not_ready; a live Gateway still starting is awaited, and outside a deploy nothing changes.
reason: S24 04/11 09:57-10:10 (deploy of 3413f27a): the Gateway died without a shutdown line under load; the Companion watchdog tried to start it every 15 s and was refused with 'Runtime lock is held by another operation' because the deploy held the lock, while the deploy waited for a readiness that could not come: gateway_not_ready, then rollback_failed with the Gateway down until the rollback relaunched it (live again 10:13:58).

tests.name: installer/termux-lite/test-runtime-sync.py
tests.evidence: 30 tests. New: an absent Gateway under the deploy lock is relaunched exactly once through --deploy-restart and then awaited (fails on the previous runtime-sync.sh: gateway stays 'unchanged'); a live openclaw-gateway process still starting is awaited, never relaunched; without the deploy lock nothing is relaunched and gateway_not_ready stays the verdict. Already registered in ci.yml.

architecture.reason: Reuses the existing deploy-restart owner (openclawGatewayClient.js --deploy-restart with the inherited lock) and the Companion's existing Gateway pid file; no new store, scheduler or daemon.

evidence: The Claw bridge depends on the Gateway and the Companion; a deploy no longer leaves the Gateway down for its whole readiness window.

limitations: Why the Gateway died at 09:57 is not proven (no shutdown line; consistent with Android killing it under memory pressure during the deploy).
The relaunch happens at most once per runtime-sync; a Gateway that dies again stays a gateway_not_ready verdict.
